- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags; adjust upward to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–2%.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias; reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., drop >3% in first 5 days), model often misses it; add early downward bias.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to lag in direction change; align forecast to sentiment swing midpoint.
